url.note: postgres:// URL; never returned by an API and never written to logs, diagnostics or support bundles

connectTimeout.constraint: whole number of seconds; injected as connect_timeout into every connection configuration

connection.loopbackException: sslmode=disable permitted only when the host is localhost or a loopback address
connection.connectTimeout: whole-second bound enforced at dial time through the driver
connection.readiness: startup waits for provider connection and required migrations before serving application traffic
connection.probe: first-run setup tests the connection and reports server version without exposing credentials
connection.diagnostics: authenticated diagnostics report provider, applied schema version and pool bound, never the DSN

schemaOwnership.sourceOfTruth: validated migration history on both providers; SQLite PRAGMA user_version is a compatibility mirror only
schemaOwnership.userIdentifiers: user collection and field names never become SQL identifiers; stable physical IDs name generated tables and columns
schemaOwnership.databaseIdentity: one provider per instance; the provider cannot be changed online after first setup

migrationBehaviour.transactionality: migration DDL and its history row commit in one transaction
migrationBehaviour.locking: PostgreSQL advisory lock on a pinned connection serializes concurrent startup
migrationBehaviour.rollback: a failed statement rolls back the entire migration; no partially recorded migration remains
migrationBehaviour.futureSchema: refused with a useful, non-secret error
migrationBehaviour.historyValidation: every version present exactly once with an authoritative name; gapped, future or malformed history fails closed
migrationBehaviour.trafficGating: no application traffic before required migrations complete
migrationBehaviour.recovery: interrupted startup resumes or fails closed with actionable redacted guidance

transactionBoundaries.perMutation: each logical mutation and its required audit record commit atomically
transactionBoundaries.isolation: ordinary operations use engine defaults; logical export uses REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY on PostgreSQL
transactionBoundaries.advisoryLocking: first-administrator setup and migration startup use PostgreSQL advisory locks
transactionBoundaries.externalEffects: remote side effects such as webhook or Lambda deliveries are deliberately non-atomic and documented

pooling.sqlite: single owned connection; not affected by PostgreSQL pool settings

timeouts.connect: whole-second bound enforced at dial time
timeouts.operation: bounded query depth, page size and result limits

cancellation.mechanism: Go context cancellation propagates to in-flight queries
cancellation.requirement: requests must not hang indefinitely or report false success

retries.transactions: no automatic retry of failed transactions at the HTTP layer
retries.idempotency: clients must use idempotency keys for retry-unsafe mutations
retries.jobs: durable job engine provides explicit retry, backoff and dead-letter state
retries.webhooks: explicit delivery retries with backoff and idempotency

backupAndRestore.portableArchive: a transactionally consistent Trestle logical archive is the cross-provider backup format
backupAndRestore.sqliteSnapshot: SQLite retains its native consistent snapshot
backupAndRestore.postgresDump: operator pg_dump or managed-cluster backup responsibilities are documented separately; the portable archive does not back up the operator's whole PostgreSQL cluster
backupAndRestore.restoreContract: restore only into an initialized, logically empty destination; all-or-nothing publication; a failed restore leaves the destination unchanged
backupAndRestore.migration: offline trestle migrate uses the portable format with a read-only source, empty-destination preflight, zero-write dry run and explicit confirmation

supported: single Trestle process with an external PostgreSQL 16, 17 or 18 service
loopback PostgreSQL without TLS for development
operator-managed pg_dump or managed-cluster backups alongside the portable archive
unsupported: SQLite on network or shared filesystems

differencesFromSQLite.connection: network service with TLS and connection pooling instead of an embedded file
differencesFromSQLite.booleans: native BOOLEAN type instead of the SQLite integer codec
differencesFromSQLite.json: TEXT with a database-level jsonb validation constraint instead of SQLite json_valid
differencesFromSQLite.nullSemantics: IS NULL / IS NOT NULL compiled through the dialect on both providers
differencesFromSQLite.jobClaiming: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED instead of the serialized SQLite claim
differencesFromSQLite.eventSequence: numeric gaps in the event sequence are not treated as missing committed events
differencesFromSQLite.migrationLocking: advisory lock on a pinned connection instead of single-process serialization
differencesFromSQLite.backup: portable logical archive with optional operator pg_dump instead of the native SQLite snapshot
differencesFromSQLite.sizeReporting: real database size instead of file bytes
differencesFromSQLite.timestampStorage: identical ordering from the shared text-timestamp contract on both providers
differencesFromSQLite.generatedIds: stable UUID identifiers on both providers

evidence.localRealService: PostgreSQL 18 exercised on a disposable local instance
evidence.ciMatrix: PostgreSQL 16, 17 and 18 in CI (historical PG12 run at 6af777b)
evidence.status: baseline green; no unresolved failures recorded at CP1
